Start Event

General Concept: A Start Event in BPMN marks the beginning of a process. It indicates where the process starts and can be triggered by various means (none, message, timer, etc.).

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a Start Event initializes the process instance and its variable scope. It supports multiple trigger types (message, timer, signal, etc.), and can be configured with input mappings using FEEL expressions. The engine ensures that all required variables are initialized and that the process starts in a consistent state.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Start Event in TaktX allows you to:

  • Trigger process start via message, timer, signal, or condition.
  • Define input mappings using FEEL expressions to initialize variables.
  • Configure error handling for missing or invalid triggers.
  • Monitor process start and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Use for event-driven or scheduled process initiation.

 

Example: Daily Report Generation with Timer Start Event

 

This example shows a process where a Timer Start Event triggers the generation of a daily report. The process starts automatically at a scheduled time, demonstrating event-driven process initiation in TaktX.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use input mappings to set initial variables.
  • Configure triggers to match business requirements.
  • Document the expected start conditions.

Pitfalls:

  • Missing or incorrect input mappings can cause process errors.
  • Unconfigured triggers may prevent the process from starting.
